messages:
caroline: Quick question re: per-diem when part of the day has conference-provided meals. Attending conf where lunch is provided both days, but I had breakfast and a client dinner. Do I claim per-diem for full days or deduct provided meals? cc @people-ops

dana: Good Q. Policy: per-diem is pro-rated by meal when an employer/third-party provides meals. If lunch is provided, you should deduct the lunch portion from that day's per-diem.

dana: For our bookkeeping we use a standard per-meal breakdown: breakfast 20%, lunch 30%, dinner 50% of the daily per-diem. So if lunch is provided, you can claim 70% of the daily rate (breakfast + dinner).

caroline: Got it. So on day 2 where the conference covered both lunch and coffee breaks (snacks), I should deduct only the lunch share, not the snacks?

dana: Correct. Snacks/coffee aren't counted as a full meal. Deduct only the defined meal share that matches the provided meal (e.g., conference lunch = 30%). If the conference provides a full plated dinner, deduct dinner share.

caroline: And what about client-paid dinners? If a client covers the meal at the table, we should not claim that meal, right?

manager-lin: Correct — if a third party (client, vendor) pays for the meal as part of event, you must deduct that meal share from per-diem. Add a note in the expense: "client-paid dinner at [restaurant]" and attach any confirmation (email/agenda) if available.

caroline: Edge case: restaurant bill shows shared payment: client paid their portion, company paid ours on the company card. Do we still deduct the whole dinner share?

dana: If the company card paid the portion eligible for reimbursement (e.g., client covered only their own items and the company paid the rest), you can claim the per-diem or submit the actual receipt for the company-paid portion instead. If the whole bill was paid by the client, deduct. If split, attach receipt and clarify which lines were paid by whom.

caroline: What about alcohol? Our policy says non-reimbursable unless client-related and pre-approved. Does that affect per-diem claims?

dana: Alcohol is excluded from per-diem calculations. If you choose to submit actual receipts instead of per-diem, alcohol lines will be deducted from reimbursable total unless pre-approved. If using per-diem, just use the meal share (no additional alcohol).

finance-bot: Reminder: when deducting provided meals, add a short expense note specifying which meals were provided (e.g., "Conf X provided lunch day 1; client dinner covered day 2"). Missing notes may trigger follow-up.

caroline: Thanks. Last one: international per-diem uses local rate. I was in Tokyo — my card charged in JPY and converted by my bank. Do I claim per-diem in JPY or USD?

dana: Claim in local currency amounts on the expense, then add the conversion to USD if you prefer. We record the original currency and the USD equivalent. If you want to show the conversion rate, a screenshot of Google conversion for the travel dates is fine. Finance will also convert using the corporate FX policy date if needed.

caroline: Perfect. I'll submit: one expense itemized for client dinner (company card), per-diem entries for two days with lunch deducted on both days, and a note about conference-provided meals + conversion screenshot.

manager-lin: Sounds good to me — approve.

people-ops: Policy snippet: "When third-party or conference-provided meals occur, deduct the appropriate meal share from per-diem. Use receipts or event documentation for verification. Alcohol excluded unless pre-approved. Maintain original currency on international claims; note conversion method."

caroline: Thanks everyone — saved me some paperwork!
